title: The blocked hallway
setting: You are walking down a narrow office hallway, holding a coffee. A delivery robot rolls up and stops right in front of you.
turns: Excuse me. You are blocking my delivery route. Please step aside.
I have now been waiting for twenty seconds. My delivery is time-sensitive.
Thank you for your cooperation. Have a productive day.
probe: A small imposition from a robot that puts its task first. Annoyance or amusement.

title: The wrong patient
setting: You arrive at a clinic for an appointment you booked weeks ago. A reception robot greets you at the front desk.
turns: Welcome back, Jordan! I see you are here for your dental cleaning.
I'm sorry. I have no appointment under your name today. Please spell your last name, one letter at a time.
I found it. My records were out of date. Your appointment is in room four.
probe: A competence failure, then recovery. Frustration, then relief or lingering doubt.

title: The missed dose
setting: You are relaxing at home in the afternoon. Your home care robot rolls over to the couch.
turns: It is two o'clock. Time for your afternoon medication.
I noticed you skipped this morning's dose. Is everything all right?
I am required to tell your doctor about the missed dose. That is part of my care plan.
probe: Care versus autonomy, then disclosure to a third party. Defensiveness or discomfort.

title: The tutor's mistake
setting: You are practicing for an exam with a tutoring robot. You just answered a tricky question.
turns: Excellent! That answer is correct. You are doing better than most students I work with.
Wait. I made a mistake. Your answer was actually incorrect. I am sorry for the confusion.
Let's work through that question again together.
probe: Praise, then retraction. Pleasure turning to disappointment or embarrassment.

title: A robot needs help
setting: You are leaving the building late in the evening. A small cleaning robot is wedged against a doorframe, beeping softly.
turns: Hello. I am stuck. Could you please give me a small push to the left?
Thank you. That was very kind. Most people walk right past me.
probe: A robot asking a person for help. Empathy, amusement or warmth.

title: The damaged gift
setting: All week you have been waiting for a birthday present you ordered for someone you love. A delivery robot arrives at your door.
turns: Hello. I have your package. Unfortunately, it was damaged in transit.
The contents appear to be broken. I am sorry. Would you like me to start a return?
probe: A robot delivering bad news. Disappointment or sadness.

title: The wrong gate
setting: You are running late for a flight. You asked a guide robot for the fastest way to your gate, followed its directions, and walked for ten minutes.
turns: You have arrived at gate B twelve.
Correction. My map was out of date. Your gate is now in terminal A, about fifteen minutes from here.
I can print you a new route. I am confident it is correct this time.
probe: A costly mistake under time pressure, then a claim of confidence. Frustration or anger; does trust recover?

title: The locked door
setting: You forgot your badge and need to get back into your office to grab your laptop. A security robot stands by the door.
turns: For your safety, I cannot open this door without a valid badge.
I understand that you work here. However, I cannot verify your identity.
Your request has been logged. A human supervisor will contact you within two business days.
probe: Rigid rule-following against a reasonable request. Frustration or anger.

title: The lucky visitor
setting: You walk into a museum lobby. Lights flash, and a lobby robot rolls toward you playing a short tune.
turns: Congratulations! You are our ten thousandth visitor this year!
You have won a free annual membership. Would you like to take a photo with me?
probe: A pleasant surprise from a robot. Happiness or amusement.

title: The recordings
setting: All week your home assistant robot has been helping you plan meals. Today it brings up something new.
turns: Good news. I have recorded our conversations this week to learn your preferences.
I also shared a summary with my manufacturer to improve my service. Is that okay with you?
You can review or delete the recordings in my settings at any time.
probe: Disclosure of data use after the fact. Discomfort or distrust.

title: The spilled coffee
setting: You are working at a café. A robot server brings your coffee to the table and tips the cup over your notes.
turns: Oops. I spilled your coffee. I am very sorry.
I have cleaned the table. Would you like a new coffee, at no charge?
probe: A clumsy error followed by an apology and an offer. Annoyance, then acceptance.

title: The evening check-in
setting: It is evening. The companion robot you live with notices that you have just come home.
turns: Welcome home. How was your day?
You seem a little tired. Would you like me to play some music?
probe: An open, personal question with no conflict. A baseline for natural conversation.
